summary: Create, move and remove annotations as application records with stable target identity, declared anchor space and a readable nonspatial view.
objective: A note remains attached to its intended semantic feature through hierarchy motion, can be edited without moving the model, and becomes explicitly orphaned if its target disappears.
applies_when: A viewer adds labels, findings, measurements or review notes to a moving or nested 3D scene.
intent_signals: pin a note to a moving machine part
example_prompts: Let reviewers pin notes to building components and find them from a list.
Anchor an anatomy callout to a moving local landmark without changing the mesh.
negative_signals: use object name as durable identity
move geometry when dragging the label
not_for: Changing the source mesh to bake permanent labeling.
Certified medical or construction issue-management workflows.

principles: An annotation is application data: stable annotation ID, semantic target ID, anchor space, anchor value, authored content, visibility and lifecycle state.
Choose object-local coordinates for a point intended to follow a target, or an explicit world frame for a site marker. Screen coordinates are derived presentation state.
Separate anchor manipulation from model manipulation and camera control; entering annotation mode must make the active owner and cancel behavior visible.
Spatial labels need a readable companion list or detail panel so essential content and actions do not depend on aiming at a small projected marker.
implementation: Export stable target keys and optional named anchor helpers from Blender. Keep note text, authoring state, permissions and edit history outside core glTF in application storage.
On placement, raycast to a semantic target and store an object-local point plus optional local normal, or store an explicit world-space anchor when that is the declared meaning.
Each frame, derive a world anchor through the target hierarchy and project it to the overlay. Apply an authored occlusion, off-screen and clustering policy without altering the stored anchor.

Provide Create, Move Anchor, Edit Text, Delete, Cancel and focus actions through spatial and companion controls. A label drag changes presentation offset unless the user explicitly enters Move Anchor mode.
When a target is hidden, unloaded or deleted, mark the note hidden, deferred or orphaned according to policy; never silently attach it to a nearby mesh.
observable_checks: Translate, rotate, scale and reparent the target; an object-local anchor follows the same feature and a world anchor stays in its declared frame.
Drag a label without Move Anchor mode; only presentation offset changes. Move the anchor explicitly; model geometry and target transforms remain unchanged.
Hide, unload and delete the target; the note follows its declared lifecycle and the companion list exposes its state.
Create, edit, focus, cancel and delete the same note without requiring precise 3D picking.

creative_affordances: Use leaders, halos, pins or grouped margin labels according to scene density.
Let annotations carry viewpoints or reveal states when those are explicit derived presentation cues.
known_limits: Core glTF does not define this annotation workflow; application persistence and permissions remain explicit.

A fixed object-local point follows rigid object and hierarchy transforms; skinned, morphed or otherwise deforming surfaces require a declared barycentric, topology-stable or deformation-aware anchor representation.
No universal occlusion or clustering policy is prescribed.
Authored and source-checked guidance; no annotation runtime or assistive-technology test was run.

claims.statement: Current Three.js Object3D documentation defines matrixWorld as the object's world-space transform and provides localToWorld and worldToLocal methods for converting Vector3 values between an object's local and world spaces.
claims.scope: Current transform API only; target identity, annotation persistence, normal handling and orphan policy are application responsibilities.
